Subject: Renewal timing + capacity add — help us align invoices

Hannah — thanks again for the demo last week. We're planning to renew in early March but need to add additional inference capacity starting Jan 1 to support a pilot. Two asks: (1) can we get a short-term top-up that bills monthly but consolidates against the March renewal invoice, and (2) what discount structure do you offer for a midterm increase that we later fold into an annual commitment?

Numbers: current committed capacity 200k tokens/mo; pilot will need +80k tokens/mo for 6 months, then likely stay at +40k thereafter. We'd prefer a simple laddered pricing approach rather than lots of one-off credits. Can you share options + an indicative number? Also attaching our renewal forecast.

Thanks — Asha

Hi Asha — appreciate the clear numbers and the spreadsheet. Quick read and initial proposal below; I'll attach a short pricing grid.

Two paths we typically recommend for this pattern:

1) Laddered top-up (recommended for pilots)
   - Jan–Jun: add 80k tokens/month as a monthly top-up at a 6% uplift discount off list for the pilot months
   - Jul onward: automatic step-down to 40k tokens/month unless you opt into the full 80k commit
   - All top-up invoices billed monthly; value of pilot months gets applied as a credit toward the Mar renewal invoice (so you won't double-pay)

2) Short co-term + annualize (recommended if you expect to keep growth)
   - Execute an amendment now for a Jan start that co-terms to your Mar renewal; we annualize the incremental capacity at a blended rate with a renewal discount (10% off blended list for incremental volume)

Looking at your shape (+80k for 6 months, then +40k), path 1 preserves flexibility and keeps uplift exposure low. Path 2 gives better unit economics once you commit to the higher baseline.

Attached: uplift_pricing_grid.csv and a draft SOW outline showing the billing treatment. If you want, I can put together a clean amendment that shows both lines side-by-side.

Next step: would you like me to model (A) monthly-topup-with-credit or (B) co-term annualize and show net invoice at renewal? I can also loop in finance for a one-time margin concession if needed.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

We're sensitive to up-front OPEX but want predictable renewal ARR. If you can show a blended renewal ARR that reflects credits, that will help the finance team.

— Asha

Hannah / Lauren — ok to be flexible here. Recommendation: offer an "escrowed conversion" structure. Key points: 

- Pilot discount: 9% for the Jan–Jun top-up (applied to the monthly top-up invoices).
- Conversion incentive: if they convert to the larger commit in March, we auto-apply an additional 3% rebate to the renewal ARR calculation (effectively 12% on the incremental volume across the blended run-rate).
- Credit treatment: pilot overpayment will be amortized across the new committed MRR (so it shows up as ARR, not a one-time line item).

Approve up to 12% effective discount on converted incremental volume. Anything beyond that needs head of revenue sign-off. Track the conversion as a delta to ARR in the HubSpot deal so finance has a single record.

Ben

Asha — thanks for the patience. Based on internal approval, here's a clean proposal: 

Proposal (pilot-first with conversion path):
1) Jan 1–Jun 30: monthly top-up of 80k tokens at 9% off list (invoices billed monthly).
2) If NovaMed converts to the larger commit at renewal (Mar 1 effective co-term), we will:
   - Apply an additional 3% conversion rebate to the incremental volume for ARR calculation (effective 12% total on converted incremental volume).
   - Amortize pilot month credits across the new committed MRR so Finance sees ARR rather than a one-off refund.
3) If you do not convert, the Jan–Jun invoices remain as billed (no retro refunds).

I've attached an updated SOW and a one-page summary. If that works, I'll prepare the amendment (co-term language + conversion clause) and the DocuSign package. Estimated impact to your Mar invoice after conversion is attached in the spreadsheet.

Next steps: confirm (a) you accept 9% pilot / 3% conversion rebate, and (b) who will sign on NovaMed's side (legal or procurement). I can run the DocuSign and target a March 1 co-term effective date.
